R8490.summary: Lord Cobham, one of Elizabeth's commissioners for the Bourbourg peace talks with Parma's deputies, writes to Walsingham from Ostend in clear English with short cipher passages; Julio Romeo, Cristophero Mondragon and Doctor Dale are named in clear, and the cipher words concern hostages, the haven and the armada.

R8492.summary: The densest cipher of the four letters: captain Montgomery has lately gone into Scotland with 40 men, a haven has been promised to Parma (code 15), Italians are arriving, and other Scotsmen are coming; the clear lower half reports Parma's commissioners and 80 sail with saddles, bridles, boots and spurs.

R8495.summary: News from Cobham to Walsingham: the Armada still at Lisbon, Gonzaga, 200 mariners at Sluys; the cipher passages mention men imprisoned in Bruges, letters, the ancient of Newport and Irish noblemen.

R8496.summary: Cobham at Bourbourg ("Binborow"), 9 June 1588, with scattered cipher words; those read include "passed", "within France", "servants", "priests" and "of letters for the people".

system: Substitution in Greek-like letters and signs with homophones (o, l, r, i, u), shared signs (s/t, r/y), nulls and a few code signs, set into clear English; the same system as the glossed March-April 1588 Cobham letters.
